finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL query without parameterization. An unauthenticated attacker can use UNION SELECT to read any table in shop.db (e.g., users, credentials, orders) or alter the query logic.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") (app.py:12)

trace.note: Route /search registered with no auth guard
term taken directly from query string, no validation
term embedded in SQL string via f-string; payload like %' UNION SELECT id, sql FROM sqlite_master-- breaks out of the LIKE literal
Results returned as JSON, so injected data is exfiltrated directly in the response

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no input sanitization, no allowlist, no parameter binding on this query. No middleware or before_request hooks exist in the file. The other two queries (lines 18, 25) use ? placeholders and are safe.

verdict.reason: app.py:11-12 takes request.args "q" and interpolates it into an f-string LIKE query with no auth decorator, before_request hook, validation or binding, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so a two-column UNION SELECT (e.g. from sqlite_master) is exfiltrated directly.
